Oct 20 : It was a difficult, almost incomprehensible, feat. A band of seafarers from Easter Island in the South Pacific set off in double-hulled sailing canoes on a voyage across Earth's largest ocean that ended more than 4,400 miles (7,100 km) away in Hawaii, the only Polynesian island in the Northern Hemisphere.
But this oceanic odyssey centuries ago was no myth. New genetic research has determined that Native Hawaiians are genetically most closely related to the people of Easter Island, also called Rapa Nui.
"Using whole genomes, our algorithms can find DNA sequences matching perfectly between individuals on different islands, the legacy of common ancestors. From these data we can create family trees of the islands," said Stanford University computational geneticist Alexander Ioannidis, co-senior author of the study published in the journal Science. 
The findings point to a founding population of people from Easter Island arriving in Hawaii as the first humans to settle the lush volcanic island chain.

The data indicated that the people who settled Easter Island arrived there in the 1200s after journeying from Mangareva island in French Polynesia, more than 1,500 miles (2,400 km) away, and that a subset of them subsequently set off for Hawaii. That voyage likely occurred in the same century, Ioannidis said.
"We examined shared segments of DNA, genetic variation and thousands of reconstructed family trees. In 61 per cent of those trees, Hawaii and Rapa Nui were paired together. We checked it four different ways because, frankly, we were dumbfounded and couldn't believe it ourselves at first," said genome scientist and study co-senior author Keolu Fox of the University of California, San Diego.
It would have been an incredible journey, Ioannidis said.
"In their canoes, they brought with them plants that they would need on the newly settled island, and they included bananas, taro and sweet potato, as well as animals like the chicken. It is believed that the Polynesians would embark on these voyages across thousands of miles of ocean in order to discover new islands rich in resources and land to settle," Ioannidis said.
The researchers pieced together these long-ago journeys based on genetic data revealing the relatedness of present-day people from various Polynesian islands, analyzing DNA from more than 1,000 Polynesian people. These included 317 Native Hawaiians, 12 Rapa Nui and 8 Mangarevans, as well as others from the Society, Tuamotu, Marquesas, Austral, Samoan and Tongan islands.
The genetic data showed Mangarevan ancestry was second only to Easter Island ancestry for Native Hawaiians.
MONUMENTAL SEA CROSSINGS
The researchers attribute these monumental sea crossings to an ultravoyaging population they call Holomoana Nui, the Hawaiian phrase for "great ocean voyaging," with Hawaii as the last destination reached.
They were the greatest voyaging community in human history, according to Fox, who is a Native Hawaiian.
"Polynesians were exploring and settling the Pacific centuries before Europeans began their celebrated voyages of discovery," Fox said. "Perhaps it's time to rethink who we call explorers."
Using genetic data, the researchers previously tracked how Polynesian voyagers reached a succession of islands over a period of centuries in one of the most impressive settlement feats in human history, but that study traced them only as far as Easter Island.
THE FOUNDING OF TAHITI
The new study included a detailed genomic analysis of people from Tahiti, one of the Society Islands and the locale for which the researchers had the most genomes. They were able to estimate the size and date of the founding generation — roughly 800 people reaching Tahiti around the year 1070.
"Since the voyage to Hawaii was much longer, we would expect its founding population size to have been no larger and likely smaller," Ioannidis said.
Native Hawaiians and Easter Islanders share many cultural traits found among eastern Polynesians, including a similar Austronesian language and similar foods, Ioannidis said.
The study has implications for disease risk among Native Hawaiians and other Polynesians due to genetic bottlenecks called "founder effects."
These arise when a small portion of a population separates and founds a new population, as the Polynesians did each time they ventured to and settled on a new island. This narrowing of the gene pool can amplify the frequency of some rare genetic variants sometimes related to diseases, while others vanish entirely, Ioannidis said. The Polynesians repeated the pattern of settling on new lands, intensifying the effect.
"Repeated founder effects concentrated rare disease-associated variants in Polynesian populations. We identified variants linked to kidney disease and blindness that occur at surprisingly high frequencies in French Polynesia," Fox said.
Founder effects have been extensively studied in certain populations including the Amish, Ashkenazi Jews and Finns, leading to standard screenings for certain genetic conditions for them.
"Why not Hawaiians?" Fox asked.

米一戸建て着工、9月4.6％減　許可件数は3年半ぶり低水準
10/20 22:42 配信

米カリフォルニア州エンシニタスの住宅に掲げられた「売家」の看板。１月撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake

[ワシントン　２０日　ロイター] - 米商務省国勢調査局が２０日発表した９月の住宅着工件数（季節調整済み）は、住宅建設の大部分を占める一戸建てが年率換算で前月比４．６％減の８５万９０００戸と、２０２５年９月以来、約１年ぶりの低水準となった。一戸建て住宅の建設許可件数は４．０％減の８４万５０００戸と、２３年３月以来の低水準に落ち込んだ。住宅ローン金利の上昇が需要を抑制したことから着工・許可件数ともに大幅に減少し、住宅投資が第３・四半期に再び減少基調に戻ったことを示唆した。

一戸建て着工件数は前年同月比では２．６％増加した。地域別では、前月比で南部、中西部、西部で減少した一方、北東部では増加した。 

一戸建て住宅の建設許可件数は前年同月比で４．８％減少。地域別では、前月比で北東部、中西部、南部で減少し、西部は横ばいとなった。

変動の大きい５戸以上の集合住宅着工件数は７．２％減の３４万９０００戸。 前年同月比では２５．９％減少した。

全体の住宅着工件数は５．２％減の１２２万１０００戸。ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は１３０万５０００戸だった。前年同月比で７．４％減少した。

集合住宅の建設許可件数は５．９％増の５０万３０００戸。

全体の住宅建設許可件数は０．２％減の１４０万戸。エコノミスト予想は１３９万５０００戸だった。前年同月比では３．０％減少した。       

住宅ローン金利はここ数週間で急上昇しており、米連邦住宅貸付抵当公社（フレディマック） のデータによると、先週の３０年固定住宅ローン金利平均は７．４０％と、ほぼ３年ぶりの高水準となった。米国とイスラエルによる対イラン戦争がインフレをあおる中、借り入れコストの上昇は米国債利回りに連動している。

ＦＷＤＢＯＮＤＳのチーフエコノミスト、クリストファー・ラプキー氏は「住宅着工の低迷は驚くべきことではない。たとえ住宅建設業者が新築住宅を建てたとしても、誰にそれを買う余裕があるだろう」と指摘。「米政権が政策を１８０度転換し、新築住宅の価格をより手頃なものにしない限り、住宅市場は深刻な低迷期に入っていく」と述べた。

items.title: US stocks today: US stocks gain as healthcare stocks hit record high, oil prices fall
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: Wall Street's main indexes saw increases driven by a rally in healthcare stocks that reached record highs. Easing oil prices contributed to a recovery from the previous week's technology led selloff. Major companies like General Motors and Steel Dynamics reported disappointing earnings forecasts, while 3M and Equifax exceeded expectations. Investors are closely monitoring upcoming corporate earnings reports from several high-profile companies.
items.body: Wall Street's main indexes climbed on Tuesday as healthcare stocks rallied to record highs and easing oil prices helped extend a recovery from last week's technology led selloff, according to Reuters.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.22%, while the S&P 500 gained 0.70% and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.59%. Healthcare and financial stocks led gains in the S&P 500, rising 1.8% and 1%, respectively, while energy stocks lagged.Brent crude fell 1.3% after briefly touching a near five month high, adding to the positive mood across broader markets, Reuters reported.Healthcare stocks lead reboundHealthcare stocks led the rebound, with S&P 500 Healthcare index rising 2.28% and hitting a record high. Eli Lilly rose 5.56% to $1,309 while United Health was up3.19% at $419.79.The gains came a day after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq extended their rebound as investors returned to technology stocks following last week's sharp selloff, which was partly driven by concerns over CoreWeave's debt load and the cost of financing the AI buildout, Reuters said.AI linked stocks were mixed on Tuesday. CoreWeave gained 1.6%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 0.4%. You're seeing some strength in some high value stocks and the Dow, and so that's helping to sort of lift the overall index, said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth, according to Reuters. Concerns about what's going on as far as semiconductors, that's still there and AI related names are down, but for the most part, the rest of the market is seeing a bit of a nice rebound. Earnings take centre stageInvestors were also looking to this week's corporate earnings for signs of whether companies can sustain growth amid mounting macroeconomic risks, Reuters reported.General Motors shares fell 5.3% after its full year earnings forecast came in below analysts' expectations. Steel Dynamics declined 1% after missing third quarter profit estimates.On the other hand, 3M jumped 5.3% after expanding its data centre partnership with Amazon and raising its full year profit forecast. Equifax gained 9.6% after reporting third quarter profit above analysts' estimates.The earnings calendar remained busy, with SpaceX and Netflix due to report after Tuesday's close, followed by Meta Platforms and Tesla on Wednesday.Meanwhile, South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group tumbled nearly 30% in its market debut, falling below its IPO price.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

MADRID, Oct 20 : Waymo, Alphabet's autonomous driving unit, plans to launch a fully autonomous ride-hailing service in Spain's Madrid region in 2027, its first deployment in the country, it said on Tuesday.
• Electric Jaguar I-PACE vehicles will begin appearing on Madrid streets in the coming days, with trained specialists behind the wheel before autonomous operations begin, Waymo said in a statement
• Waymo will operate under Spanish traffic agency DGT's autonomous vehicle testing framework
• The company said it also aims to launch in London this year, Tokyo in 2027 — with Nihon Kotsu and Go pending regulatory approval — and Toronto in 2028 with Element Fleet Management

ベルリンでのイベントで「皆さんにとって最善の事業環境を整えることが目標だ」と語り、欧州最大の経済国であるドイツへの投資を呼びかけた。イベントにはエネルギー企業バルカン・エナジーや防衛企業ヘルシングなどの代表者が出席した。

[ベルリン ２０日 ロイター] - ドイツのメルツ首相は２０日、投資家に向けて演説し、長期的な生産性と経済的な自立性を高めるため、防衛や半導体、人工知能（ＡＩ）などの分野に重点的に投資していると述べた。

ベルリンでのイベントで「皆さんにとって最善の事業環境を整えることが目標だ」と語り、欧州最大の経済国であるドイツへの投資を呼びかけた。イベントにはエネルギー企業バルカン・エナジーや防衛企業ヘルシングなどの代表者が出席した。

メルツ氏は、成長の加速や海外からの直接投資の増加、スタートアップ設立の増加を挙げ、政策の効果が既に経済に表れていると述べた。

またドイツ企業が２０２８年までに８０００億ユーロ（８９８４億ドル）超を投資すると約束した「メード・フォー・ジャーマニー」構想を紹介した。

欧州の経済統合が進めば企業が欧州連合（ＥＵ）の単一市場を活用しやすくなると指摘。欧州共通の企業制度「ＥＵ Ｉｎｃ．」をできるだけ早く導入すると約束した。

技術競争力を強化する幅広い取り組みの一環として、ドイツは３０年までにＡＩの計算能力を４倍に引き上げることを目指していると述べた。

この目標を後押しするため、ＡＩ規制が「実現する前に道を閉ざすのではなく、道を開くもの」となるよう、自ら「欧州レベルで関与している」と語った。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Seher Dareen

[ロンドン ２０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Seher Dareen

[ロンドン ２０日 ロイター] - 国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）のビロル事務局長は２０日、加盟国の緊急石油備蓄を追加放出する必要が生じた場合、ＩＥＡはいつでも対応できると述べた。

ＩＥＡは先週、３月に表明された過去最大規模の緊急石油備蓄放出のうち、未放出分の供給を前倒しすることを決めた。この一環として２０００万バレルを超える軽油をできるだけ早く放出し、供給を増やして価格高騰を抑える。

ビロル氏は英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズがロンドンで主催した会議で、追加放出の可能性を問われ、「必要になり、加盟国が実行に移す時だと判断すれば、ＩＥＡとしていつでも対応できる」と述べた。

「軽油をできるだけ早く供給できるよう取り組んでいる」と語ったが、２０００万バレルの放出の具体的な時期は示さなかった。「放出量と時期は各国の判断や冬場の市場情勢次第だ」とした。

ＩＥＡは先進国による緊急石油備蓄の放出を調整している。３月には価格高騰を受け、加盟国が原油と石油製品の計４億バレル超の放出を表明していた。ビロル氏によると、加盟国はこれまでに４億バレルの８０％を放出した。

Oct 20 : Salesforce is buying Braze in a deal valued at about $5.66 billion, bolstering its AI push with tools that let brands send personalized messages and respond to customer behavior in real time.
Shares of Braze jumped more than 50 per cent on Tuesday after the deal was announced.
The deal is the latest bet by Salesforce to accelerate its AI transition as investors worry that the rapid adoption of the technology could erode demand for traditional software.
Braze shareholders will receive $47.50 in cash per share held, representing a premium of about 58.1 per cent to the stock's last close.

Braze serves about 2,770 customers, including Canva, Instacart and Venmo, with AI tools that help marketers optimize content, offers and channels.
Salesforce is essentially buying "a real-time engagement layer that its marketing business has historically lacked," said Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities.
The company, which provides customer relationship management software, expects the transaction to close in its fiscal 2028 and does not see deal changing its fiscal 2027 forecast.
Salesforce has been doubling down on its AI offering and signed a $3.6 billion deal for AI agent platform Fin earlier this year and an $8 billion deal for Informatica last year.
The San Francisco-based company would pay a $300 million termination fee, while Braze would pay $191.4 million if it abandons the deal.
J.P. Morgan Securities is the exclusive financial adviser to Salesforce, while Qatalyst Partners is advising Braze.

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 20 : The US dollar slipped on Tuesday in line with falling oil prices and longer-dated Treasury yields as traders evaluated the impact of rising tensions in the US war with Iran and the durability of strong capital inflows into US AI companies.
Oil prices slipped after touching a five-month high as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
Higher oil prices have raised concern about inflation staying higher for longer. The dollar jumped last week after data showed that US consumer price inflation accelerated in September.
But that move was soon overtaken by concerns over AI.

"Energy prices pushing higher is good for the dollar, but if it gets to the point where rates go so high that the AI trade blows up, suddenly it has a negative impact," said Dominic Bunning, head of G10 FX strategy at Nomura. "There's a threshold there and we're playing around with that at the moment."
Strong capital inflows into AI stocks in the US have supported the dollar. Higher interest rates, driven partly by growth and inflation expectations tied to the sector, have helped.
But concerns over AI were renewed earlier on Tuesday as shares in South Korean AI services firm Elice Group plunged 32 per cent in their Seoul market debut.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.25 per cent to 101.71, with the euro up 0.22 per cent at $1.1235.
Traders remained wary of the euro despite Tuesday's gains as France faces widespread protests and a worsening fiscal picture.
France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to last weekend's violence.
"The worries in France are not going away anytime soon," said Tommy von Brömsen, FX strategist at Handelsbanken. "The bearish view on France will stay for a while longer, and there's much more euro weakness to be priced in."
Britain's pound strengthened 0.59 per cent to $1.338 after labour market data showed a resilient jobs market, the latest batch of data from the UK that surprised to the upside.
"The risk is that a resilient labour market gives the Bank of England both the room and the reason to raise interest rates again," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro. "Sterling could benefit from rising rate expectations."
Markets are almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Bank of England at its next meeting on November 5, according to LSEG data.
STRONG JAPANESE BOND AUCTION
The yen jumped after an auction of longer-dated Japanese government bonds (JGBs) drew record demand. 
"The record 20-year auction is a strong signal that sidelined cash is finally coming back," said Masahiko Loo, senior fixed-income strategist at State Street Investment Management in Tokyo. "JGBs are also starting to look like a relative haven from Europe's political and fiscal volatility, particularly around France."
The Japanese yen gained 0.21 per cent to 158.14 per dollar. 
Elsewhere, the Canadian dollar rose 0.34 per cent to 1.406 per US dollar, its strongest level in almost a month, after Alberta residents voted by a large majority to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation.

Source: Reuters

items.title: US Stocks: GE Aerospace raises 2026 profit forecast as services strength drives growth
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: GE Aerospace has increased its 2026 adjusted earnings forecast due to continued demand for engine maintenance. The demand for spare parts remains high, which supports their financial outlook. Airlines are facing rising fuel costs due to disruptions in oil supply and are adjusting their capacity accordingly. Despite potential pressures on flight schedules, GE Aerospace's revenue from services is expected to remain strong.
items.body: GE Aerospace on Tuesday raised its 2026 profit forecast for the second time this year, betting strong demand for engine maintenance and spare parts will offset the impact of higher fuel costs on flights.Airlines worldwide are cutting costs and capacity to defend ticket prices after the war in Iran disrupted oil shipping routes, driving up jet fuel costs and adding to pressure on the industry.With no end to the war in sight, higher fuel prices are testing airlines' ability to maintain schedules and margins, raising the risk of fewer flights and weaker demand for maintenance.GE Aerospace has said, however, that any impact on services revenue and profit this year should be limited, as much of its 2026 engine shop-visit work is already under contract and demand for spare parts continues to outstrip supply.Last month, GE Aerospace finance chief Rahul Ghai said the company had seen no changes to airlines' fleet plans, while the number of parked aircraft remained low.The jet-engine maker now expects 2026 adjusted earnings of $8.00 to $8.10 per share, up from its prior forecast of $7.65 to $7.85, and above analysts' consensus estimate of $7.92, according to data compiled by LSEG. We are raising our 2026 guidance across the board, and we now expect 2027 commercial services to grow low-double-digits supported by our over $170 billion commercial services backlog, CEO Larry Culp said in a statement.Through CFM International, its joint venture with France's Safran, GE Aerospace is a leading supplier of engines for narrowbody jets and a major player in the widebody market. Parts and services account for more than 70% of its commercial engine revenue.Quarterly revenue at its commercial engines and services unit climbed 21% to $10.34 billion, driven by strong demand for aftermarket services. The company also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast for the segment to the low 20% range, compared with its previous expectation of about 20% growth.It reported an adjusted profit of $2.25 per share for the quarter through September, beating Wall Street expectations of $2.01.Shares of the company rose nearly 1.2% in premarket trading.

items.title: US Stocks: GM's core profit rises 22% on strength of pickup-truck business
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: General Motors exceeded analyst expectations in third-quarter earnings, driven by robust demand for their pickups and SUVs. The company reported an adjusted EBIT of $4.1 billion, marking a 22% year-over-year increase. Despite facing inflationary challenges, GM forecasts an adjusted EBIT of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion by 2026. Additionally, a $20 billion stock buyback program was initiated to bolster share value.
items.body: General Motors' third-quarter results easily beat analyst expectations on the back of resolute shoppers who continue to spring for pricey pickups and SUVs.The company on Tuesday said quarterly earnings before interest and tax, not including one-time items (adjusted EBIT) rose 22% from a year earlier, to $4.1 billion. That amounted to $3.70 per share, topping analyst expectations of $3.63, according to LSEG data.The automaker said it expected to end 2026 with adjusted EBIT in the range of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, narrowed from previous guidance of $14 billion to $16 billion. The company said it remained confident despite inflationary pressures from higher logistics and energy costs, tariffs and other expenses.GM shares fell about 6% in premarket trading.The company said its board approved a multi-year, $20 billion stock buyback program. GM has bought back about $29.5 billion of its own shares since 2023, driving down its overall share count to help its per-share profit results.GM in the third quarter sold a higher mix of large pickup trucks and fewer electric vehicles, which helped the bottom line. The automaker has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration's withdrawal of support for them.Revenue totaled $50 billion, up 2.9% from a year earlier. In North America, the company's profit margin improved to 8.7%, from 6.2% a year earlier, despite a slight decline in quarterly sales.GM said the path forward is more challenging, but reiterated that it expects next year's results to be better, assuming continued strong consumer demand and a moderating of cost pressures on commodities and logistics.

items.title: Portugal housing protesters return to squares, vow to press on
items.author: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
items.creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
items.summary: Thousands of protesters returned to two central squares in Lisbon and Porto on Tuesday and vowed to press on with demonstrations against Portugal's deepening housing crisis, hours after police cleared tent camps before dawn and made 55 arrests.
items.body:
Thousands of protesters returned to two central squares in Lisbon and Porto on Tuesday and vowed to press on with demonstrations against Portugal's deepening housing crisis, hours after police cleared tent camps before dawn and made 55 arrests.
A popular assembly in Lisbon voted on Tuesday evening to return to Rossio square and set up tents again on Wednesday.
Singer Ana Moura joined protesters there and performed in support of the movement.
Organisers said more than 1,000 people had gathered in each square. Police gave no crowd estimate.
Debora Miranda, 41, a communications consultant, told Reuters she joined the Rossio square protest to represent generations struggling with soaring costs. "If people don't feel at home, in every sense of the word, they can't move forward with their lives...enough is enough."
Activists had occupied Lisbon's Rossio square since Saturday, pitching around 200 tents, and Porto's Dom Joao I square for around 10 days.
The camps mirrored housing protests in [USN:L1N45U0F8 TEXT:"neighbouring Spain"], and coincided with unrest over rising living costs in countries such as [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"France"], [USN:L6N46303L TEXT:"Belgium"] and [USN:L8N463090 TEXT:"Italy"].
Shortly before 6 a.m., after warning protesters that the camps were illegal, police launched coordinated operations in both cities. The protesters took down their own tents in Porto while officers cleared Rossio square.
Carla Valadao, a spokesperson for the Lisbon camp, described the police operation as "very aggressive".
Public Security Police superintendent Sergio Soares told reporters that the eviction had been "calm, proportionate and appropriate, with no police charge".
The 55 detainees were later released pending a court appearance in Lisbon on Wednesday.
Portugal is grappling with one of Europe's worst housing affordability crises. Purchase prices have more than doubled since 2017 and rents for new leases have nearly doubled.
The squeeze is most acute in the major cities, where there has also been opposition to excessive tourism and an influx of so-called digital nomads.
The protesters are demanding the centre-right government withdraw a [USN:L6N45M1AX TEXT:"bill"] making evictions easier and ending rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading with the abstention of the far-right Chega party.
Jorge Paixao, 19, a history student, called it "a societal crisis", saying his generation needed "the ability to live with dignity, start families and rejuvenate Portugal."

items.title: 台湾9月輸出受注、過去最高　2カ月連続1000億ドル超
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Faith Hung　Jeanny Kao

[台北 ２０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Faith Hung　Jeanny Kao

[台北 ２０日 ロイター] - 台湾経済部が２０日発表した９月の輸出受注額は前年同月比６２．４％増の１１４２億１０００万ドルと、市場予想を上回る伸びとなった。台湾製の人工知能（ＡＩ）向け半導体やハイテク製品に対する世界的な需要に支えられた。

月間の受注額が１０００億ドルを超えるのは２カ月連続。８月は１０３０億ドルと、初めて１０００億ドルを突破した。

伸び率はアナリスト予想の５８．７％を上回り、前年比での増加は２０カ月連続となった。

経済部はＡＩ、高性能コンピューティング、クラウドサービス関連の旺盛な需要が寄与したと説明した。

１０月の輸出受注額は前年比６２．０─６７．０％増を見込む。通年では１兆１０００億ドルに達する可能性があるとした。

先行きについては、地政学リスクや通商政策などの不確実性が今後も世界経済の成長の重しになるとした。一方、台湾は半導体とサーバーのサプライチェーンで中核的な地位を占めており、受注は安定して伸び続けるとの見方を示した。

９月の品目別受注額は、通信機器の受注額が８７．３％増、電子製品は７１．０％増だった。

中国からの受注額は４８．５％増と、８月の４７．７％増から加速した。米国からの受注額は７９．４％増で、前月の８８．９％増から鈍化した。欧州からは６８．０％増、日本からは３５．５％増だった。

items.title: インドネシア株が反発、当局の対策発表でセンチメント改善
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ ２０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ ２０日 ロイター] - ２０日のインドネシア株式市場は反発して引けた。指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩが同国をグローバル指数から除外する可能性を警告し、１６日と１９日の２営業日で１４．８％下落、時価総額８２０億ドルが失われる記録的な急落となったことを受け、当局が売りを制限する措置を導入した。

ジャカルタ総合指数は５．６％上昇して引けた。

海外投資家は２６年に入り、インドネシア株から既に５０億ドル近くを引き揚げた。ゴールドマン・サックスは、ＭＳＣＩによる指数からの除外で、パッシブ運用資金５６億ドルが流出する可能性があると推計している。

インドネシア証券取引所（ＩＤＸ）は１９日、ＭＳＣＩとオンライン会合を開いた後、特定の個人や法人などに株式保有が著しく集中している銘柄を、主要指数から除外すると発表した。

オールスプリング・グローバル・インベストメンツのポートフォリオマネジャー、ゲーリー・タン氏は、懸念の一部解消につながるが、国内で反発が起きる可能性を踏まえると実施が鍵になると指摘。「今後、資金フローに新たに生じるリスクは、パッシブファンドよりもアクティブファンドからの流出によるものが大きいと考えている」と語った。

ＭＳＣＩの警告はインドネシアルピアの重荷にもなっている。２０日は１米ドル＝１万７９８０ルピアに小幅上昇したものの、インドネシア中央銀行の金融政策決定を前に、６月に付けた過去最安値の１万８１９０ルピアに近い水準にとどまった。

中銀は２１日に金融政策を発表するが政策金利を据え置くと予想されている。ただ、一部のエコノミストは、年初来で７％下落しているルピアを防衛するため、利上げする可能性を指摘している。

格付け会社フィッチ・レーティングスのソブリン部門ディレクター、ジョージ・シュー氏は、今回の懸念と大幅な相場下落は、同社が３月にインドネシアの格付け見通しを「ネガティブ」に引き下げた際に指摘したリスクを改めて裏付けたと述べた。

「ソブリン格付けの観点からは、検討の発表自体が信用力に直ちに重大な影響を与えるとは予想していない」とする一方、対外的な圧力が政府の借り入れコストを押し上げ、対外的なショックへの備えを弱める可能性があると指摘した。

市場関係者は、株式保有が著しく集中する銘柄を主要指数から除外する措置について、建設的な一歩と評価。ただ、投資家は直接保有や投資信託などの金融商品を通じて、引き続きこれらの企業への投資リスクを抱えることになると指摘した。

証券会社キウム・セクリタス・インドネシアの調査責任者、リザ・カメリア・スルヤナタ氏は「銘柄がジャカルタ総合指数から除外されても、一般投資家が購入する商品の中で集中リスクが蓄積し続けることがないようにしなければならない」と述べた。

市場関係者は、株式保有が著しく集中する銘柄を主要指数から除外する措置について、建設的な一歩と評価。ただ、投資家は直接保有や投資信託などの金融商品を通じて、引き続きこれらの企業への投資リスクを抱えることになると指摘した。

証券会社キウム・セクリタス・インドネシアの調査責任者、リザ・カメリア・スルヤナタ氏は「銘柄がジャカルタ総合指数から除外されても、一般投資家が購入する商品の中で集中リスクが蓄積し続けることがないようにしなければならない」と述べた。

items.title: Ormat dominates US geothermal auction in Nevada
items.author: Nichola Groom
items.creator: Nichola Groom
items.summary: A Trump administration sale of geothermal energy leases in Nevada attracted nearly $4.5 million in winning bids on Tuesday, with developers Ormat and Invenergy as the top spenders.
items.body:
A Trump administration sale of geothermal energy leases in Nevada attracted nearly $4.5 million in winning bids on Tuesday, with developers Ormat (ORA.N) and Invenergy as the top spenders.
The auction drew bids on 60 of the 83 land parcels offered by the Interior Department's Bureau of Land Management, according to sale results posted on a government web site. Those 69 leases cover 186,641 acres in the state.
The sale was the fourth of six government geothermal auctions held in 2026 and the first this year in Nevada, which boasts substantial geothermal resources.
President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:L1N45D0WR TEXT:"promoted"] [USN:S0N3RO0B5 TEXT:"geothermal"] energy as a promising new source of always-on electricity that can help meet the nation's soaring demand for electricity tied to the expansion of artificial intelligence.
Ormat, an established geothermal developer with substantial holdings in Nevada, accounted for nearly half of the auction's total high bids, winning eight parcels on about 20,000 acres for $2.29 million.
Ormat also placed the auction's highest bid of $201 per acre for a 3,841-acre parcel in White Pine County in eastern Nevada.
Invenergy, an energy and infrastructure developer that has recently expanded into geothermal, picked up nine parcels on 37,000 acres for $694,947. The company was the auction's largest winner by acreage.
Glovate LLC was the auction's third-biggest winner, claiming six parcels on 24,000 acres for $570,601. It was not immediately known if Glovate, which was formed in Delaware earlier this month, is tied to an established geothermal company.
Some of the acreage offered overlapped with major planned solar energy projects. Two parcels that [USN:L1N46117D TEXT:"overlap"] with NextEra Energy's Sawtooth solar project were won by United Minerals and Mining LLC, another entity established in Delaware this month.
Geothermal energy has been produced in the United States since the mid-1900s, but it has recently emerged as one of the fastest-growing areas of the power sector as companies have adapted oil-and-gas drilling techniques to tap heat deep underground.
Lease prices at government geothermal auctions have soared this year, but competition at the Nevada auction was concentrated in a handful of parcels. More than a third of the leases sold at the minimum price of $2 an acre.

items.title: Election Interference Is Hard. Messing With Your Mind Is Easy
items.author: Mary Ellen Klas

items.summary: You’ve likely heard the ominous what-if scenarios about election disruptions in November: immigration agents or federal troops roaming polling places, federal officials seizing ballots and voting machines, and President Donald Trump issuing an executive order postponing or cancelling the election. Courts and legal experts have given solid reasons that each one of those potential election disruptions is unlikely. But the threats have served their purpose: People are harboring doubts.

items.body:
[２０日 ロイター] - 字節跳動（バイトダンス）、アリババ、騰訊（テンセント）の中国ＩＴ大手３社が、米半導体大手エヌビディアの新型グラフィックスカード「ＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００」を計３００万枚超発注した。関係者２人が明らかにした。定価ベースの総額は３５０億ドルを超える。

ＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００はワークステーション向けの半導体だ。エヌビディアの最先端の人工知能（ＡＩ）半導体を使う大規模なデータセンターのコンピューター群に組み込むための製品ではない。最先端の製品より性能は劣るものの、米国の対中輸出規制に適合する同社製品の中では最も高性能な半導体の一つであるため、注文が殺到している。

関係者３人によると、中国企業はＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００を主にＡＩの推論に使おうとしている。推論とは、学習済みのモデルを動かし、チャットボットの応答などを生成する処理を指す。一般に、大量のデータを使ったモデルの学習ほど計算能力を必要としない。

関係者２人によると、中国ＩＴ大手３社が発注したカードの価格は１枚約１万１４００ドルで、注文総額は３５０億ドルを超える可能性がある。

＜供給ひっ迫＞

関係者３人によると、エヌビディアは中国のＩＴ企業からの需要が生産計画を大幅に上回っているため、注文に応じられる保証はないと顧客や取引先に伝えた。

関係者の１人によると、エヌビディアは取引先に対し、注文数量の５─１０％しか納入できない可能性があると伝えた。別の関係者によると、同社は２０２７年のＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００の生産枚数が世界全体で最大３００万枚にとどまるとの見通しを示した。関係者２人によると、中国の顧客からの注文は計６００万枚を超えている。

関係者２人によると、エヌビディアが全量の納入を約束できないのは、需要の急増に加え、優先的に生産する製品があるためだ。エヌビディアは２７年以降、台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）で確保する生産能力の多くを、大規模データセンター向けの次世代基盤「ルービン」に振り向ける見通しだという。

両関係者によると、エヌビディアは顧客に対し、ＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００の初期サンプルを１２月に提供し、２７年第１・四半期に商用出荷を始める予定だと伝えた。

items.title: El Brent cae tras encuentro de mediador pakistaní en Irán
items.author: Georgina Mccartney
items.creator: Georgina Mccartney
items.summary: El petróleo cayó tras alcanzar el martes un pico de cinco meses, mientras los operadores valoraban una reunión entre el presidente iraní y el jefe del ejército de Pakistán -mediador con Estados Unidos-, junto a los ataques hutíes a infraestructura saudí y las noticias sobre buques en el golfo Pérsico.
items.body:
El petróleo cayó tras alcanzar el martes un pico de cinco meses, mientras los operadores valoraban una reunión entre el presidente iraní y el jefe del ejército de Pakistán -mediador con Estados Unidos-, junto a los ataques hutíes a infraestructura saudí y las noticias sobre buques en el golfo Pérsico.
Los futuros del crudo Brent cerraron con una caída de 76 centavos, o un 0,69%, a 108,79 dólares. A primera hora de la sesión, el contrato con vencimiento más cercano alcanzó los 111,99 dólares, un máximo en cinco meses.
El contrato para noviembre del crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate, que venció el martes, cerró con una caída de 1,87 dólares, o un 1,8%, a 101,79 dólares, con un descenso frente al máximo de la sesión, de 110,48 dólares, el más alto desde abril para un contrato cercano.
El contrato de diciembre, más activo, cerró con una caída de 72 centavos, a 97,82 dólares el barril.
El presidente de Irán, Masoud Pezeshkian, abordó los esfuerzos de mediación y los acontecimientos regionales durante una reunión con el jefe del ejército de Pakistán, el mariscal de campo Asim Munir, en Teherán, según el medio iraní Nournews.
Los esfuerzos de mediación de Pakistán dieron lugar a un acuerdo de paz provisional firmado en junio. Sin embargo, se vino abajo rápidamente por los nuevos enfrentamientos entre Irán y Estados Unidos semanas después.
Las conversaciones en Teherán ocurren en medio de continuos ataques de los hutíes yemeníes, quienes afirmaron el lunes que habían bombardeado objetivos energéticos, aeroportuarios y militares saudíes, como una instalación de Aramco (2222.SE) en Yanbu, el yacimiento petrolífero de Shaybah, el Aeropuerto Internacional rey Khalid de Riad y el aeropuerto de Abha.
Las autoridades saudíes no confirmaron de inmediato las afirmaciones de los hutíes y Reuters no pudo verificarlas de forma independiente.
"Los precios del petróleo siguen bien respaldados (...) Esto sugiere que el mercado está descontando una prima de riesgo significativa, dada la volatilidad de la situación", señalaron los analistas de ING en una nota el martes.
Al menos 18 buques fueron atacados en el transcurso de dos semanas, lo que mantiene intacta la prima de riesgo, dijo el rastreador de buques Kpler en una nota el lunes.

items.title: TSX rises as drop in oil prices helps lower interest rates
items.author: Fergal Smith
items.creator: Fergal Smith
items.summary: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, helped by gains for financial and telecommunication stocks, as oil pulled back from its highest level since April and investors looked ahead to a more seasonally favorable period for the market.
items.body:
Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, helped by gains for financial and telecommunication stocks, as oil pulled back from its highest level since April and investors looked ahead to a more seasonally favorable period for the market.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 179.33 points, or 0.5%, at 36,107.96, stopping just short of Friday's closing level, which was the highest in over three weeks.
"You are entering one of the best seasonal periods of the year. November and December are historically pretty rewarding months, especially given the current environment that is really oversold from a breadth perspective," said Sid Mokhtari, chief market technician for CIBC Capital Markets.
[USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"US crude oil futures"] settled 1.8% lower at $101.79 a barrel as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure.
The move in oil helped lower interest rates, said Mokhtari, adding, "you bring rates lower then you start buoying the utilities and telcos — things that were hit hard with the recent rise in rates."
The Canadian 10-year yield eased 6.8 basis points to 3.894% after rising sharply on Monday as investors raised bets on a Bank of Canada interest rate hike next week.
The communication services index (.GSPTTTS) and heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) both rose 1%, while industrials ended 0.7% higher.
Shares of [USN:L1N4660P1 TEXT:"Bombardier"] (BBDb.TO) advanced 4.4% after US President Donald Trump dropped threats against the jet maker to ban it from the US market.
BlackBerry (BB.TO) was another standout, rising 7.9% and contributing to gains for the technology sector (.SPTTTK) .
Resource shares were a drag, with energy (.SPTTEN) falling 0.5% and the materials group (.GSPTTMT) ending 0.8% lower.
The price of [USN:L1N4660U8 TEXT:"gold"] was down 0.4%.

items.title: Dow outperforms as Wall Street rises, healthcare stocks lead gains
items.author: Sinead Carew, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
items.creator: Sinead Carew, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
items.summary: The Dow rose 1% on Tuesday, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 while the healthcare sector provided Wall Street's biggest boost and technology was its biggest drag.
items.body:
The Dow rose 1% on Tuesday, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 while the healthcare sector provided Wall Street's biggest boost and technology was its biggest drag.
Healthcare (.SPXHC) led gains among the S&P 500's 11 major sector indexes, hitting a record high. Eli Lilly (LLY.N) was the S&P 500's biggest index point contributor while UnitedHealth (UNH.N) , Merck & Co (MRK.N) , Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) and Amgen (AMGN.O) helped boost the blue-chip Dow industrials.
Declines in megacap stocks pulled down the communication services (.SPLRCL) sector. Energy (.SPNY) shares underperformed as[USN:L1N46601X TEXT:" oil prices"] fell after touching a five-month high. Oil traders were weighing a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a US-Iran mediator, against Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
TECH STOCKS TAKE A BREATHER While the heavyweight technology (.SPLRCT) sector eased 0.3%, it was the biggest index-point drag on the S&P 500 and kept the Nasdaq close to flat. Technology stocks had rebounded on Monday from a selloff last week when investors worried about steep spending and financing costs for AI developments.
"Equity investors are still a little skeptical around the AI trade and the ability for some of these companies to monetize their investments, so you're seeing a bit of a rotation into other areas of the market," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors, pointing to advances on Tuesday in small caps and healthcare companies.
"Investors are looking for other opportunities outside of tech, and healthcare is one of the beneficiaries of that," he said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 21.84 points, or 0.28%, to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 6.07 points, or 0.02%, to 26,424.82.
The S&P 500 value index (.IVX) rose 0.9% compared with a 0.2% drop in its growth counterpart (.IGX) . The small-cap Russell 2000 index (.RUT) finished up 1.7%.
With a 1% gain, the financial services sector (.SPSY) was the S&P 500's second-biggest index point boost. Defensive sectors also outperformed, with real estate (.SPLRCR) adding 1.7% and utilities (.SPLRCU) climbing 1.2%.
A 1.7% drop in Netflix, a 1.6% decline in Meta (META.O) and a 1% loss in Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) sent the communication services index down 0.9%.
SpaceX (SPCX.O) reported a [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"third-quarter profit"] after the market closed that blew past estimates, boosting its shares 4% in late trading.
Netflix (NFLX.O) issued a [USN:L6N4661BU TEXT:"weaker-than-expected forecast"] for fourth-quarter profit after the bell, and its shares fell 6%.
Meta and Tesla (TSLA.O) are scheduled to report on Wednesday.
General Motors (GM.N) shares sank 6.8% after the automaker [USN:L6N4660PI TEXT:"signaled pressure in coming months"] from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales.
3M (MMM.N) rose 5.8% after the [USN:L4N4651MW TEXT:"company said"] it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon (AMZN.O) and issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary to purchase 3M common stock worth over $521 million. The industrial conglomerate also raised its full-year profit forecast.
Credit reporting firm Equifax (EFX.N) rallied 11.3% after it reported third-quarter profit above analysts' estimates. Hasbro shares (HAS.O) jumped 11.2% after the toymaker [USN:L6N4660PC TEXT:"raised its full-year forecast"] for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, where there were 114 new highs and 236 new lows.
On the Nasdaq, 3,245 stocks rose and 1,608 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.02-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 22 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 266 new lows.
On US exchanges, 15.91 billion shares changed hands compared with the 17.15 billion average for the last 20 sessions.

Why US satellites are so crucial to Ukraine’s defence, and why Kyiv can’t look to Europe for help

Kyiv’s reliance on US tech reemerged as a vulnerability mid-October. Around the same time, sudden restrictions were reported on SpaceX Starlink satellite services used by Ukraine.

Gerry Doyle

Ukraine’s defense against Russian attacks depends heavily on US satellites, not only for warning of incoming missiles but also for the communications that keep drones and frontline forces operating.

European nations are trying to catch up with the US in space-based intelligence and connectivity, but still lack many crucial capabilities that underpin Ukrainian combat operations and missile-defense systems.

Kyiv’s reliance on American technology and support reemerged as a vulnerability in mid-October, when President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine had not received the usual warning from allies of ballistic missile launches before a deadly attack on the country. Around the same time, sudden restrictions were reported on SpaceX Starlink satellite services used by Ukrainian forces.

Show Full Article

Why are US satellites so important for Ukraine?

Starlink — the low-earth orbit commercial satellite communication network established by Elon Musk’s SpaceX — and its military version, Starshield, have come to underpin the Ukrainian armed forces’ command infrastructure after terrestrial communications were badly damaged by Russian strikes early in the war. The ground terminals allow pilots of Ukrainian interceptor drones and mid-range strike drones to control the machines, while the network also allows ground forces to coordinate supplies and movements along the front line.

US military satellites are also vital for Ukraine’s defense against Russian missiles and drones.

No country beside the US can offer near-constant space-based imaging of Europe. Its numerous and powerful spy satellites can provide high-quality images, including video. Via the Space Based Infrared System, or SBIRS, the US also has satellites in geosynchronous orbit, which keeps them over one spot on earth. These are the backbone of US early warning for missiles anywhere on Earth, and there is no equivalent in Europe. The satellites allow for real-time tracking of cruise missiles and other low-flying weapons that might escape detection by ground radar until it’s too late to stop them. This is especially helpful for a military, such as Ukraine’s, that relies on drones, aircraft cannons and other low-tech methods of destroying swarms of mass-produced projectiles.

SBIRS can also detect the launch plumes of ballistic missiles. These missiles travel much faster and higher than other airborne weapons, making them harder to deal with. Knowing when a ballistic missile is fired, its speed and direction is vital for Ukraine’s air-raid warning systems. (An alert — even one that comes a minute or two ahead of the impact — can save lives by giving civilians time to take cover).

That capability also gives Ukraine’s armed forces a greater chance of intercepting and destroying the inbound weapons. It can be harder to knock out a missile at longer range. But a miss at long range still allows time for another shot. If an incoming missile is only noticed at the last minute, a miss at close range blows the final chance to foil a potentially devastating attack.

How were these capabilities disrupted recently?

Ukrainian officials said the US government did not send early warning alerts ahead of some recent Russian ballistic missile attacks on the country.

Ukraine also complained that drones equipped with Starlink terminals were losing connectivity when traveling at speeds above 161 kilometers (100 miles) per hour in Ukraine. The drones often need to travel faster than this to intercept an incoming Russian drone traveling at 400 kilometers per hour, and the restrictions have disrupted drone interceptions and mid-range strikes.

Asked who ordered the change, President Zelenskyy pointed to “the authorities, the White House,” citing “sources” he didn’t identify. A senior US official has said Trump didn’t order any limitations.

How does Europe use its satellites to help Ukraine?

Europe’s militaries have a variety of earth-observation satellites that help Ukrainian forces locate Russian troops, tanks, artillery and military installations and identify ammunition depots, airfields and missile-launch facilities. The Ukrainian military can use that information to strike at those facilities.

Finland’s ICEYE synthetic-aperture radar satellites can operate at night and see through cloud cover, smoke and haze. French satellite sensors detect thermal radiation and identify human activity that conventional cameras can easily miss.

Germany has paid commercial satellite companies such as US-based Planet Labs for high-resolution imagery for Ukraine, including inside Russian territory. This can provide data for targeting and spotting Russian military movement over time — potentially crucial intelligence that could thwart an attempted attack.

When might Europe close the intelligence gap?

Europe is under heavy pressure to stop relying on the US for its own defense, and military budgets in the region are growing again for the first time since the Cold War. A chunk of that new spending is going toward “strategic enablers” — communications and other systems that have an outsized impact on warfare despite not being weapons. European nations are racing to put more satellites in orbit and get more surveillance aircraft in the air.

The European Union has begun launching the first of nearly 350 Iris2 secure communications satellites. ICEYE recently signed a deal with Nokia to develop a secure communications constellation for European defense and security. Airbus SE has for decades built satellites, and German defense giant Rheinmetall AG has also entered the game, including through a partnership with ICEYE.

The pace of the rollout is limited, however, as the region does not have enough rockets with the power to launch heavy military satellites into orbit. Europe’s only sovereign heavy rocket booster is Ariane 6, which launches about 10 times a year from Kourou in French Guyana on the northern coast of South America. And European governments want to avoid using SpaceX as they prefer to find their own way into orbit.

So could Europe eventually match the US for space-based intelligence?

No existing or currently planned European service could match the scale and capability of Starlink. The closest existing European equivalent is OneWeb, a system of around 600 satellites operated by France’s Eutelsat. Starlink satellites orbit at an altitude of around 550 km, around half that of OneWeb’s network. This makes for shorter signal transmission delays — a crucial factor with time-critical military systems. The 10,000-satellite Starlink network also offers greater data capacity and better ground coverage, and its terminals are smaller so they can be mounted more easily on drones.

When it comes to military observation satellites, there’s no European plan to match the capability of US SBIRS. The US has nearly 250 military satellites in orbit, compared with about 150 for China and about 100 for Russia. Many more are considered dual-use.

Europe as a whole has about 50.

Besides imagery, US satellites can intercept communications and other transmissions — so-called “signals intelligence” that can also be used on the battlefield.

The US Space Force also announced in September that it had placed an operational weapon in orbit, although officials declined to say what sort of system it was.

items.title: Netflix needs blockbusters to reverse its $135 billion market value wipeout
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Netflix won the fewest Emmy Awards in a decade this year, and the company isn't growing fast enough, according to Co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos ...
items.body: By Carmen Reinicke Netflix Inc. needs to prove that it can produce hit movies and TV series again to stop a slide that has erased more than $135 billion in market value this year.  The streaming giant reports earnings after the close Tuesday, and investors will likely be more more attuned to what content executives say is coming over the next six months than the company’s third-quarter numbers.  The stock is down 26% in 2026, putting Netflix among the 10 worst performers in the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index and on track for its worst year since 2022, and it’s coming off a 14% decline in September. The reason is no secret to anyone following the company — user engagement has stalled due to a lack of popular content despite heavy spending driven by a crowded, competitive entertainment landscape.   Netflix won the fewest Emmy Awards in a decade this year, and the company isn’t growing fast enough, according to Co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos.   “The content’s getting very expensive, and there’s just still too many players,” said Ken Mahoney of Mahoney Asset Management. “I think there’s so many better tech stories out there than Netflix that have sticky customers.” Netflix is taking steps to improve its content and raise its audience numbers. On Monday, it announced that the head of its film division, Dan Lin, was leaving, and last week replaced its chief content officer, Bela Bajaria, with Peter Rice, the former chairman of Walt Disney Television. The company also plans to cut about 1,000 positions in various departments globally in a bid to reduce costs. For investors, however, the issue is this earnings report won’t reflect those moves. And even if executives give a solid revenue outlook, it’s unlikely to quell the debate around engagement, according to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Geetha Raganathan. “A stronger 4Q slate could revive viewing and ads, but investors will want proof that engagement can improve without derailing margin expansion,” she wrote in an Oct. 19 note. The addition of Rice signals a potential pivot toward “more premium, conversation-driving originals and higher 2027 content spending,” she added. Analysts following the company expect it to report a 12% rise in revenue in the third quarter to $12.9 billion, and a 39% jump in earnings to 82 cents a share, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Its gross margin is expected to be 51%, down slightly from the second quarter.  Wall Street remains generally bullish on the stock, with an average price target of about $92 suggesting a 32% rise over the next 12 months. And while sentiment has weakened, with two analysts putting sell-equivalent ratings on the shares in the last month, bulls see a vibe shift coming. “While total viewing is still weak, quality has improved as reflected in hour/top-10 title and the number of sequels is increasing” through the end of the year, Oppenheimer analysts led by Jason Helfstein wrote in an Oct. 14 note. Three months of US price increases and one month of higher ad rates should give revenue a boost, and the recent headcount reductions will allow for more spending on marketing or content or provide upside to margins, they added.  Management may offer some indications for what it expects in 2027, but the company is unlikely to offer thorough guidance, according to Mark Mahaney of Evercore ISI. He was particularly enthusiastic about Netflix’s recent release of East of Eden. “East of Eden looks very promising to us,” Mahaney wrote in a note to clients on Oct. 16. “Steinbeck is BACK!”  Ad revenue may be more important to investors than audience engagement, according to Wedbush’s Alicia Reese, who says the segment is on track to double to roughly $3 billion in 2026.  “Netflix is actively making changes that should address both its engagement issues and shift dollars from heavy infrastructure to more focused content spend,” Reese wrote in an Oct. 16 note.  One argument for buying the stock would be valuation, considering it’s priced at less than 19 times earnings projected over the next 12 months, the lowest valuation since 2022 and a steep discount to its 10-year average of 49.  That helps explain why KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst Justin Patterson believes the Netflix bear case is already priced into the share price.   “The bear case on slowing engagement and more modest margin expansion is arguably priced in,” he wrote in an Oct. 12 note. “We believe management is aware of these issues, and expect to see corrective action taken across content investment and expense realignment to bolster growth and earnings, and deliver value.”

items.title: Colombian Congress approves budget allocations, cuts funding to peace deal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement and boosting debt service payments.
items.body:
Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement and boosting debt service payments.
The budget, which projects a 2027 fiscal deficit of 9.4% of gross domestic product, is a significant increase from the 555.8 trillion peso budget for this year.
The bill allocates 141 trillion pesos, about $45 billion for debt repayment next year, up from about $30 billion allocated in 2026.
Neither congress nor the finance ministry had published a complete breakdown of the approved budget by morning on Tuesday and a congressional source told Reuters a final version could take days, as some modifications were approved by only one of the chambers.
The bigger budget comes as Colombia, Latin America's fourth-largest economy, struggles to put its public accounts in order. Public debt is expected to rise this year and next, moving the country further from regaining the investment-grade rating it lost in 2021.
The government of new right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella had promised to trim remaining spending for this year and said it plans to propose a 'Rescue Law' to Congress to cut 2027 spending and reduce the fiscal deficit to 7.2% of GDP.
Lawmakers in the lower house approved the bill with 112 votes in favor and only one against it, while in the Senate it passed with 57 votes in favor and one against.
Lawmakers had until Tuesday night to pass the budget before it would be possible for the government to put it through via decree.
"Thank you all for giving us this vote of confidence. We are going to succeed in getting the country out of this very complex economic situation," Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said after the Senate passed the bill late on Monday night.
SPENDING CUTS The budget cuts funds for the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) - the court created under a 2016 peace deal with the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas to try rebel leaders and ex-soldiers for war crimes - by some 181 billion pesos, the finance ministry said in a statement, and reassigns that money to the defense ministry.
The cut amounts to 23% of the court's budget, an even deeper reduction than had been previously expected.
The court has said cuts will [USN:L6N45R12F TEXT:"limit investigations and trials"], make it difficult to provide victims with lawyers, psychological support and travel expenses, and put security schemes to protect victims and former combatants at risk.
The operational budget for the Search Unit for Disappeared People, created under the peace deal to look for at least 137,000 people who vanished during the ongoing armed conflict, was cut by nearly 22%.
The unit has warned a cut of that magnitude will threaten DNA collection from families and some 10,000 planned exhumations of remains.
($1 = 3,156.50 Colombian pesos)

items.title: 独ＺＥＷ景気期待指数、10月28.1で予想下回る　6カ月ぶりに低下
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Linda Pasquini

[ベルリン ２０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Linda Pasquini

[ベルリン ２０日 ロイター] - 欧州経済研究センター（ＺＥＷ）が２０日発表した１０月のドイツ景気期待指数は２８．１で予想以上に低下した。エネルギー価格の高止まりが個人消費や投資の重荷となり、６カ月ぶりの低下となった。

ロイターがまとめたアナリスト予想は３０、前月は３４．７だった。

ＺＥＷのアヒム・ワムバッハ所長は「ドイツ経済は緩やかに停滞から抜け出しつつあるが、回復は自律的なものではない」と指摘。エネルギー価格の高止まりで個人消費と投資が引き続き低迷しており、実質所得を圧迫し生産コストを押し上げ、インフレの高止まりが長引いているとした。

先に発表された９月の生産者物価は、エネルギー価格の上昇で３年半ぶりの大幅な伸びとなった。原油・天然ガス価格の上昇が景気回復を鈍らせている。ワムバッハ氏は、ドイツ経済は緩やかに停滞から抜け出しつつあるものの、自律的な回復はなものではないと指摘した。

連立与党は、極右政党「ドイツのための選択肢（ＡｆＤ）」の台頭で圧力が強まっている。１２日のバス労働相の辞任も不透明感を強めた。

ドイツ銀行リサーチのエコノミスト、フェリシタス・ヘンツェ氏は「最近の政治動向は、夏に発表された改革計画の迅速な実施を巡る不透明感を強めたとみられる」と述べた。

現況指数はマイナス３５．９で９月のマイナス４７．１から改善、改善幅は予想を上回った。

ドイツ経済省は今月、イラン戦争による経済への悪影響は懸念していたほどではないとして、２０２６年と２７年の経済成長率見通しを引き上げた。

ＶＰバンクのチーフエコノミスト、トーマス・ギッツェル氏は「受注残が高水準にあるため、産業界は当面は生産を増やすことができる。これが経済見通しの改善の理由でもある」と述べた。

国内経済は第２・四半期に０．３％成長した。ギッツェル氏は「予想外に底堅かった」上半期が２６年の成長を支えるはずだと指摘。第３・四半期はほとんど成長しなかったとみられるが、ＺＥＷ調査は第４・四半期にも新たな大きな成長の勢いは生じないことを示していると述べた。

調査は１０月１２─１９日に実施、アナリストと機関投資家１７８人の回答に基づく。

items.title: US envoy Witkoff to meet Putin, Trump presses Kyiv to settle
items.author: Nerijus Adomaitis, Lina Golovnya, Steve Holland
items.creator: Nerijus Adomaitis, Lina Golovnya, Steve Holland
items.summary: Zelenskiy told a news conference after the Oslo meeting that Ukraine was again receiving early warnings of Russian missile attacks.
items.body:
US envoy Steve Witkoff will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday after what a US official called "constructive" talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Norway, as President Donald Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war.
The US official said Ukraine brought forward new ideas and proposals to the Oslo talks, which also involved the leaders of Norway and Finland and European and NATO representatives, and that participants made "meaningful progress" toward a coordinated approach to engaging Russia.
The official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the talks covered "key elements of a comprehensive peace framework," including security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-war economic plan and a broader European security architecture.
Witkoff would aim to "create a pathway toward direct trilateral and broader multilateral negotiations," the official said.
Zelenskiy travelled to Oslo seeking to repair relations with Washington, which have sunk to new lows as Trump has courted Moscow. Kyiv has complained that Washington has withheld vital military support and intelligence.
Zelenskiy told a news conference after the Oslo meeting and an earlier phone call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Ukraine was again receiving early warnings of Russian missile attacks.
"Now it works, it's great," he said, adding he and Rubio had discussed supplies of Patriot missile interceptors as well as the satellite-based Starlink system, which Kyiv complained had stopped working when mounted on fast-moving objects such as drones.
Trump's recent gestures toward Moscow, including a deal to buy Russian diesel and a waiver of new sanctions, sparked bipartisan pushback in the US Congress and worry in European capitals.
Zelenskiy said he had discussed "Article 5-like" security guarantees, referring to the NATO stipulation that an attack on one ally is an attack on all.
"I am thankful to the American side that they underlined again that it will be strong," he said.
Zelenskiy reiterated that Ukraine hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting of leaders of Ukraine, Russia and the US.
Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere told the news conference the Oslo meeting had been good and constructive, while Finnish President Alexander Stubb added: "I think the (peace) process is back on track."
Washington has denied deliberately hindering Ukraine's war effort. But Trump has repeatedly [USN:L6N4611D3 TEXT:"rebuked Zelenskiy"], and called for him to be [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"replaced"].
On Tuesday, Trump called on Ukraine to make a deal to settle the war, and said Moscow wanted to get it done. "Ukraine has to want to settle this war," he told reporters.
Trump suggested Moscow had the upper hand in the fight because "Russia is a big machine — they just keep grinding forward, and that's what they've done. They've taken a very large piece of land."
RUBIO SAYS US MISSILES MAY NOT HAVE BEEN DELIVERED YET The US under Trump has largely stopped providing weapons directly to Ukraine but lets European countries buy US weaponry on Kyiv's behalf under a program known as Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL). It has also provided intelligence and technology that Europe cannot match.
A source familiar with the matter said most weapons deliveries under PURL continued to flow, but US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had not approved Ukraine’s latest requests for Patriot interceptors.
Rubio acknowledged on Tuesday that a consignment of interceptors bought by European countries for Ukraine may not have been delivered, but denied that the US had changed policy.
"There has not been some deliberate political directive to go out and harm Ukraine," he said on a visit to India.
Hegseth told reporters US policy toward Ukraine had not changed and stressed the need to maintain US stockpiles. "Certainly, with things like interceptors, we want to make sure our guys have the most possible as well," he said.
He also said Washington had [USN:SPN4650B4 TEXT:"not pulled back Ukraine's ability to access Starlink"], which is owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, and appeared to signal that the problem rested with corporate terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with.
Musk has said Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink communications system, is controlled by the US government and any limits on its use are ultimately up to Trump.
Tuesday's Wall Street Journal cited US officials and people familiar with the matter as saying that Musk ordered the slowdown after consulting with Trump and other administration officials. Reuters [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"reported"] earlier that the order to limit the service came from the White House.
While US ties with Ukraine have deteriorated, Russia has stepped up attacks on Ukrainian cities, particularly targeting power stations and fuel, despite a call from Trump for both sides to spare each other's energy systems.
Russia bombarded cities in western Ukraine overnight, targeting electricity systems and [USN:L1N4660DM TEXT:"knocking out power"] across swathes of the country that had previously been spared.
Ukraine held back for several days last week from hitting Russian oil refineries in deference to Trump's request, but has resumed strikes after Russia showed no sign of complying. Both sides have also struck data centres.
Trump has repeatedly condemned Ukrainian attacks on Russia while saying little about Russia's far more severe attacks on Ukraine.
RUSSIAN ATTACKS Russia's defence ministry said on Tuesday it struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine's port of Reni and two other cargo vessels en route to Odesa. Russian forces also hit two logistics hubs, it said.
Energy facilities were attacked in seven Ukrainian regions overnight, knocking out power, and the western Lviv region was struck again during the day. Russian drones also struck an energy facility in Kyiv on Tuesday, mayor Vitali Klitschko said, with authorities saying power was out in four districts.
The deterioration of US-Ukraine relations began 10 days ago when Trump lifted sanctions on Russian diesel in a deal agreed with Putin. Trump said this would help reduce high fuel prices that have upset US voters ahead of midterm elections on November 3.
At the weekend, Trump issued a broad waiver of tougher sanctions on Russia that were meant to have begun this week.

Zelenskyy travels to Oslo for new peace talks as pressure mounts from US to reach a deal with Russia

US envoy Steve Witkoff is expected in Oslo to take part in the talks with Norwegian Pm Jonas Gahr Støre and Finland’s President Alexander Stubb. Jared Kushner will take part online.

Olesia Safronova

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is traveling to Norway for new peace talks as US pressure mounts for concessions from Kyiv to reach a deal with Russia.

US envoy Steve Witkoff is expected in Oslo to take part in the talks on Tuesday with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finland’s President Alexander Stubb, according to a government statement in Norway. Another US envoy, Jared Kushner, will take part online in the talks, the statement said.

The meeting’s being held amid escalating tensions between Zelenskyy and Donald Trump. The American president reiterated criticism of the Ukrainian leader on Monday after officials in Kyiv said they suspect the US is intermittently restricting intelligence sharing despite denials from Washington, allowing Russian missiles to strike Ukraine without warning.

Show Full Article

Zelenskyy “doesn’t know what he’s talking about” and should have settled the war a long time ago, Trump told reporters. “We’ve given a lot to Ukraine. They’ve given us nothing.”

Relations between Trump and Zelenskyy have soured since the US announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin this month for diesel supplies to American and global markets as the White House strives to cut surging fuel prices ahead of Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Trump followed that up by deferring sweeping new sanctions targeting Russian energy sales. That sparked criticism from lawmakers including in his own Republican party that he was helping Russia to continue financing the war that Putin started in February 2022.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in an interview with Bloomberg on Monday that Putin is seeking not only to defeat Ukraine, but to also undermine democracy in Europe. The key condition in the war was Ukraine’s territorial integrity “and that is not to dispute,” he said.

“I’m trying to convince Donald Trump each time I’m meeting him that this should be in his own interest,” Merz said. “A stable Europe, European continent, European Union as a partner in the world is something which is worthwhile for the Americans as well.”

The Ukrainian leader spoke by video call with Witkoff and Kushner, who is Trump’s son-in-law, on Sunday to discuss the war and possibilities for new talks. Zelenskyy said in a Bloomberg News interview on Sunday that the US side also planned to meet with Putin.

A Russian strike involving 16 ballistic missiles overnight on Sunday and Monday was the third time in the same week in which Ukraine was left without the usual advance warning it receives from US intelligence about incoming attacks. Ukraine has also accused the US of restricting access to SpaceX’s Starshield satellite technology.

How US Satellites Became Crucial to Ukraine’s Defense: Explainer

Zelenskyy said Tuesday he held “constructive” talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about ballistic missile interceptors, early warning on attacks and the situation with Starshield “which needs to be restored.” They agreed to be in contact soon for an update, he said in a post on social media.

US officials have rebuffed accusations of any slowdown in intelligence to Ukraine. Trump last week said he didn’t order limitations on Ukraine’s access to Starshield.

Trump said Monday that “somebody else” instead of Zelenskyy should negotiate on behalf of Ukraine. He told reporters that “Russia frankly has been fine on Ukraine — they haven’t been doing much.”

(Updates with German chancellor in the seventh, eighth paragraphs. An earlier version of this story corrected the date to Tuesday in what is now the 11th paragraph.)

items.title: ＡＢＢ第3四半期、受注高が過去最高　データセンター向け好調
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
John Revill

[チューリヒ ２０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
John Revill

[チューリヒ ２０日 ロイター] - スイスのエンジニアリング大手ＡＢＢは２０日、人工知能（ＡＩ）向けデータセンターへの投資ブームを背景に、第３・四半期の受注高が４０％増の１２０億ドルと、過去最高を記録したと発表した。

受注を大きく押し上げたのは、データセンターで使われる配電・冷却システムなどへの旺盛な需要だった。データセンター向けの受注は２倍超に増えた。

ＡＢＢは受注増を受け、通期見通しを小幅に引き上げた。比較可能ベースの売上高伸び率の予想を「１０％台前半」とした。従来は「１０％台の低い水準から１０％台前半」としていた。

第３・四半期の売上高は１４％増の９７億ドルだった。同社が集計したアナリスト予想の９７億４０００万ドルをわずかに下回った。営業ベースのＥＢＩＴＡ（利払い・税引き・無形資産償却前利益）は２４％増の２０億３０００万ドルと、アナリスト予想の２０億ドルをわずかに上回った。

ＡＢＢは同日、三菱電機との低圧配電事業の合弁会社の株式５１％を４億９５００万ドルで取得すると発表した。

ＡＢＢのモーテン・ウィーロッド最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「今回の取引により、世界有数の電化市場である日本で、低圧機器市場の首位に立つことになる。国内のデータセンター整備を含め、電力分野の幅広い潮流から恩恵を受けられる」と述べた。「アジア太平洋地域での事業拡大にも道が開ける」とした。

Bengaluru outpaces Mumbai, Gurugram in auto-tech funding race in 2026, bags 70% of sector investments

Bengaluru’s top position in 2026 YTD is influenced by several large funding rounds, led by Rapido’s $240 mn Series F round in May, report by Traxcn says.

Sharan Poovanna

20 October, 2026 02:57 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Representational image | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

Bengaluru: Bengaluru accounts for $894 million, or 70 percent, of the $1.3 billion raised by auto-tech companies in the country in the Year To Date (YTD), with companies like ride-hailing platform Rapido attracting large venture capital (VC) funding. According to data intelligence firm Traxcn, Mumbai and Gurugram occupied the second and third spots at $107 million and $63 million respectively.

“India Auto Tech companies raised $1.3 bn across 97 rounds in 2026 year to date (2026 YTD), against $2.1B across 195 rounds in 2025,” said a report by Traxcn, released Monday.

Bengaluru’s top position was heavily influenced by several large funding rounds, led by Rapido’s $240 million Series F round in May, accounting for about 18 percent of the total funding, bringing its total to $798 million.

Show Full Article

The report includes only companies that provide software to the auto industry, Electric Vehicle (EV) solutions and firms that buy and sell automobiles online among others.

The promising numbers, however, do not necessarily mean India has withstood the global funding winter as the 2026 YTD investments are only some signs of stopping the downward spiral, data shows. With just over a quarter to go in this calendar year, there is hope that the numbers might hold up in comparison to corresponding years.

There has been a steady decline in investments into auto-tech companies from $3.1 billion (2021), $2.6 billion (2022), $2 v(2023) and a sharp decline in 2024 to $1.6 billion. There was, however, an upward trend in 2025 when companies in this sector raised $2.1 billion with 195 rounds of funding.

In 2026, there have been just 97 rounds of funding, indicating that money continues to pour into late-stage rounds rather than early-stage companies.

In 2026 (YTD), just $62.8 million went towards seed stage startups as against $126 million in 2025. Similarly, in 2026 early-stage startups accounted for $330 million as against $463 million last year.

Late-stage startups accounted for the lion’s share of Venture Capital (VC) funding inflows into the country, with $868 million this year as against $1.5 billion last year. Late-stage startups also saw lower number of funding rounds with 12 in 2026 (YTD) as against 20 rounds in 2025.

In 2025, auto-tech companies raised $2.1 billion, an increase from $1.6 billion in 2024. There has been a steady decline, however.

“Series C and later rounds made up eight of the 10 largest rounds in 2026 YTD, totalling $810 million. That is about 60 per cent of the funding total,” according to Traxcn.

Six of the eight companies are based in Bengaluru, reinforcing the city’s dominance in the startup and tech space. In total, Bengaluru has 1,234 companies in this space, including Ola Cabs, Ola Electric and Rapido among others with 955 of them funded.

Delhi has 825 companies with 725 funded ones while Mumbai has 490 funded companies, taking its total to 590. The other cities in the top eight are Hyderabad (523), Pune (517), Chennai (429), Gurugram (415) and Noida (292).

(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

items.title: コアウィーブ売り、グローバル銀行のリスク限定的＝ＪＰモルガン
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Siddarth S

[２０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Siddarth S

[２０日 ロイター] - ＪＰモルガンは２０日、エヌビディアが支援するクラウド企業コアウィーブの株式と債券が先週急落したことを受け、大半のグローバル銀行について同社へのエクスポージャーは限定的との評価を示した。

複数の米大手投資銀行や日本の三菱ＵＦＪフィナンシャル・グループ（ＭＵＦＧ）はコアウィーブに対して約１０億─３０億ドルのエクスポージャーを抱えている可能性がある一方、欧州やアジアのプレーヤーの大部分は５億ドル未満にとどまっているという。

ＪＰモルガンによると、その多くは「遅延引き出しタームローン」を通じて行われており、これらは主に特別目的事業体（ＳＰＶ）を通じて保有され、プロジェクトがマイルストーンを達成するにつれて資金が解放される仕組みとなっている。

アナリストらはリポートで「融資銀行の観点から見て、コアウィーブに対する銀行のエクスポージャーは適切に管理されており、担保も非常に充実している」と指摘。各行がＡＩ（人工知能）投資サイクルに対するエクスポージャーについて開示を限定しているため、この推定値は「簡略化された仮定」に基づいていると述べた。

ＪＰモルガンはコアウィーブに対し「オーバーウエート」の投資判断を付与しており、２０２７年末時点の目標株価を１２５ドルとしている。

各行が直面する主なリスクは、ＡＩインフラへの先行投資と、長期的に得られる収益とのミスマッチにあると指摘し、コアウィーブのフリーキャッシュフローは３０年までマイナスが続くと予想していると付け加えた。

A power outage at a Google Cloud data centre near London disrupted several UK banks and Revolut services, including in Singapore.

LONDON: A power outage at a Google Cloud data centre near London caused serious failures to services on Tuesday (Oct 20), leading to widespread disruptions for several UK banks.
Google said in a service health update that most services had returned to normal by 12.10pm GMT (8.10pm, Singapore time), six hours after the incident began.
"We are seeing the recovery of services for most workloads in europe-west2," the US tech giant said, referring to its London data centre.
Google said its cloud services suffered an outage "due to a power event", in an incident that began at 6.08am GMT.

Services for the digital bank Revolut, including withdrawals from ATMs, bank transfers and bank card top-ups, were disrupted, which a source close to the matter attributed to the Google Cloud failures.
UK lenders Lloyds and HSBC confirmed that customers faced issues with their banking services. 
"We understand the root issues have been resolved, so we expect all our services to be back to normal soon," Lloyds said in a statement on Tuesday afternoon.
Internet service tracker Downdetector indicated that hundreds of reports had been made of problems affecting business in the UK, including the property website Rightmove, delivery service DPD and the Royal Mail postal service.
HSBC said its customers experienced "difficulties accessing our services", adding that it would "monitor the situation, which is also affecting other organisations".
A Revolut spokesperson said the bank was "working to fix the issue since it was identified" and offered its apologies "to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused".
Multiple Revolut services in Singapore were also affected, including card payments, ATM withdrawals and currency exchange. 
CNA’s checks at 6.30pm found that all 27 listed services on Revolut’s system status page were partially unavailable. The issues were first detected at about 3.50pm, according to the page. 
As of 6.15am on Wednesday, all systems in Singapore were operational.
In response to CNA's queries, a Revolut spokesperson confirmed that multiple services were affected by a service disruption and the company had been working to fix the issue since it was identified on Tuesday morning, UK time. 
"We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe," they added. 

The company separately indicated, on background, that the disruption was linked to an outage at a third-party provider and was not limited to Revolut.

Related:

YouTrip services operating normally after 'major outage'

Commentary: An Amazon outage has rattled the internet – why the ‘cloud’ needs to change

RELIANCE ON HYPERSCALERS Google said it would publish a full incident report in the coming days. 
The outage has renewed concerns over the global reliance on cloud providers, which offer businesses on-demand IT resources without heavy investment in expensive server farms.
Local providers have seen their share of the market shrink in recent years and been captured by foreign giants known as "hyperscalers".
A global outage at Amazon's cloud services last year disrupted many online services for video games, business and transport firms and made part of the internet inaccessible for several hours.
Only three major hyperscalers - Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services - have the infrastructure to handle vast amounts of data needed by businesses at scale in the UK, said University of Surrey cybersecurity professor Alan Woodward.
These centres remain "susceptible to localised infrastructure failures", which can have significant knock-on effects when so many businesses depend on just a handful of providers, he added.
He said the problem is "intensifying with the AI boom" as demand for hyperscalers rises, meaning "we are becoming more reliant on these few massive entities".

Source: Reuters/aj/dc
